newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hits new session low after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hits new session low after U.S. data.

text.p: IPE Brent crude slipped to a new session low on Wednesday as the release of U.S. inventory data confirmed the early bearish tone, brokers said.

U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) data released on Wednesday showed crude oil stocks rose by 2.6 million barrels last week. Middle distillate stocks were up by 1.6 million barrels and gasoline by 200,000 barrels.
"The DOE has basically confirmed the bearish tone on crude and distillates but not for gasoline," said a broker.
June Brent shed 27 cents to $17.87 a barrel by 1433 GMT, just four cents above the intraday low posted moments earlier.
American Petroleum Institute (API) figures issued on Tuesday showed similar builds in crude and middle distillates but a 3.63 million-barrel rise in gasoline stocks.
On Wednesday, the API said U.S. gasoline supply this summer should be more than enough to meet even the most bullish forecasts of peak demand growth.

"In our view, gasoline supply has the potential to grow enough this summer in order to accommodate even the higher 2.5 percent rate of growth suggested by our upper-bound demand estimate," the API said in its annual outlook for the summer peak driving season.
Brokers said Brent crude was vulnerable to further losses, having broken below technical support at $17.91 a barrel, and pegged the next level of support at $17.80 a barrel.
In the gas oil pit, meanwhile, prompt May futures also lost ground, shedding $2.75 to $162.50 a tonne by 1443 GMT after dipping as low as $162.00.
"It's broken through support at $162.25. If it goes below $162 then we could be heading for $160.75," said a broker.
Volume on both gas oil and Brent remained depressed, partly in response to Tuesday's May Brent expiry, brokers said.
